title: Rapid prompt ingest lanes: tokenize fast-path + selective KV prewarm to cut prefill overhead
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce CPU and wall-time overhead on the prefill path by introducing a split tokenizer ingestion design (fast lane for common short prompts and cached prefixes + slow lane for heavy tokenization), coupled with selective KV prewarm heuristics and tighter kernel-selection signals. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout for the ingestion lanes and the prewarm scheduler so hosted and Dedicated customers see lower end-to-end prefill latency and lower per-token CPU cost.

Background: Recent e2e traces show that for short prompts (<64 chars) up to 40% of request latency is spent in prompt normalization + tokenization + prefix lookup; multi-tenant CPU contention amplifies this. Meanwhile, some common prefixes (system prompts, onboarding banners) are repeatedly tokenized across requests. We can reduce both repeated work and tail latency by: (1) a lightweight, branchless fast-path tokenizer for common short prompts and cached prefixes, (2) an async prefill prewarm stage that warms hot KV entries for predicted decode trajectories, and (3) exposing kernel-selection hints (short-context fused-attention) earlier in the pipeline so the serving runtime can pick better kernels before full prefill completes.
acceptance_criteria: Fast-path tokenization enabled behind flag and opt-in routes
End-to-end p50 prefill latency reduction >= 1.8x for short prompts (<64 chars)
CPU cycles used by tokenizer for common prompts reduced by >= 30%
No regression in generation quality or tokenization correctness (automated token diffs)
design_decisions: Two-lane ingestion: 'fast' lane uses a light tokenizer + fingerprint cache; 'slow' lane uses full tokenizer with normalization and locale handling
Cache keyed by (model_id, customer_id (when present), prefix_hash, tokenizer_version)
Selective KV prewarm uses a 95th-percentile decode heuristic: prewarm top-K next-token KV shards when decode branching probability > threshold
Expose 'short_context' kernel hint in prefill RPC to influence kernel selection for small sequence lengths
implementation_notes: Implement fast tokenizer as a C++ microkernel with SIMD-friendly lookup table; fallback to Python/CPP tokenizer for edge cases
Cache size target: 2M entries global with per-region LRU shards; soft TTL 10m for prefix entries
Prewarm runs at most one async prefill per request to avoid over-saturating GPU; rate-limited by per-customer budget
Add telemetry events: ingest_lane, prefix_cache_hit, prewarm_triggered, prewarm_success, kernel_hint_emitted
benchmarks: Dev cluster: short_prompt_synth: baseline p50=26ms, p95=84ms -> fast-lane p50=9ms, p95=52ms (2.9x p50 improvement)
CPU profile: tokenizer CPU cycles for 256K samples reduced 35% after enabling cached-prefix lookup
End-to-end throughput: small prompt tail improvement under 75% load on Dedicated pools
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cache poisoning via crafted inputs -> mitigation: canonicalize and limit cacheable content to non-user-inserted system prefixes by default
Risk: prewarm causes unwanted GPU work -> mitigation: conservative thresholding, per-customer rate limits, and opt-out flag for low-trust tenants
Risk: tokenizer divergence across versions -> mitigation: include tokenizer_version in cache key and invalidate on tokenizer releases
work_items: Add prefix fingerprint service + LRU shard (infra tasks coordinated with ENG-5120)
Integrate kernel_hint field into prefill protobuf and runtime router (proto change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/protos/pull/128)
E2E perf run on staging and Dedicated smoke tests
